chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
"What is the least by which a servant becomes a disbeliever?" He said: "That he innovates something in it, then he adheres to it and disassociates himself from those who oppose it."

key_terms.مَنْ خَالَفَهُ: those who oppose him / differ from him
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: adheres to it / turns to it

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum condition for a Muslim to be considered a disbeliever according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the threshold for major disbelief is defined not merely by holding a novel view, but by the combination of introducing an innovation (bid'ah), firm adherence to it, and disassociation (tabarru') from opponents. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'ta'assub' (partisan zeal) and the severing of ties with the Ahl al-Bayt's followers as a critical marker of kufr, distinguishing it from simple error. The hadith underscores that intellectual deviation becomes spiritual ruin when accompanied by exclusive loyalty to the innovation and rejection of the truth.
